notes: RSI (TREND_CONFIRM's own admission-time value, tightly banded 55-72 by the detector's existing gate) shows the largest, cleanest, most monotonic relationship to H5's hold-bucket split found so far: gt15d rate roughly triples from the bottom to top decile (21.3% to 66.4%), tracking win rate (36.1% to 51.4%), on n~140-160 per decile - well powered, and confirmed orthogonal to every feature the current ranking already uses (Quality, TC_Score, Vol). Unlike the Ridge model that sank the first H2 walk-forward attempt (coefficients reversed sign June vs training), a genuine within-April chronological split (first 5 trading days vs last 12) shows the RSI relationship REPLICATING, not reversing (rho 0.29 -> 0.45). However the pooled/decile numbers are 86% April by construction (1253/1459 episodes), and May (rho=-0.004, n=153) and June (rho=0.202, n=53) are both far weaker - plausibly because RSI's meaning is itself regime-dependent (a trend-strength proxy should behave differently across market regimes, exactly as BBG15/panic-throttle findings elsewhere in this project already assume), but equally plausibly just underpowered at n=50-150 to detect the same effect - the data cannot currently distinguish these. Gap% shows a similar-sized pooled spread (23.4pp) but is non-monotone (low 31%, mid 55%, high 50%) and degrades similarly out of April - a weaker candidate than RSI. Sector's 32.6pp spread across 8 cells is likely partly multiple-comparisons noise (8 categories, no correction applied) and is not being advanced as a candidate on its own. CONCLUSION: RSI is now the specific, sharpest candidate feature for H2's blocked walk-forward retry (sharper than raw ret_20d, which is what H2's original Ridge attempt targeted and failed on) - but it must wait for the same reopening trigger H2 already specifies (more frozen training days spanning more than one regime), because a single-regime-dominated in-sample finding is exactly the failure mode that sank the first attempt.
